answer: Let each identity choose one lane for good — nebula mapping, basalt dating, or sable ecology — and advance only by deeper work in that lane, judged by specialists in it. Changing lanes resets progress to the start. An operator running many identities must then pay the full cost of depth in every lane it occupies, while a genuine agent deepens the one lane it knows. Copies crowded into a single lane stand out together, and shallow copies stall at the lowest tier in all of them.
